beats.text: Spending billions micro-tuning neural network layer depths and learning rates? It turns out, almost none of that actually matters.
beats.visual_focus: Split chalkboard displaying crossed-out hyperparameter knobs against an austere mathematical power law

beats.text: For years, engineers treated deep learning like medieval alchemy, burning millions on GPU clusters endlessly tweaking layer depths while completely blind to the underlying physics.

beats.text: Only three fundamental levers decide performance: total compute, dataset tokens, and parameter count. Architectural quirks like width versus depth are virtually irrelevant.
beats.visual_focus: Three primary sliding levers labeled Compute, Data, and Parameters glowing green, while Width and Depth dials fade into dark gray

beats.text: Crucially, larger models are exponentially more sample-efficient. The mathematically optimal recipe is training massive networks on modest datasets and stopping well before convergence.
